meta.review: machine-written (Claude): the tables, the partners and the animate nouns; not reviewed by a native speaker. Checked against Fran (2026-10-30, docs/plans/05-built/native-check-sl.md): the noun tables by Slovenski pravopis 2001 (fran.si) and their full paradigms first on Sloleks 2.0's site (viri.cjvt.si/sloleks), then against the Sloleks 3.0 release (CC BY-SA 4.0, http://hdl.handle.net/11356/1745; 2026-11-04, docs/plans/05-built/cleanup-code.md): a note citing 3.0 holds no form it lacks, one still citing the site holds a form it lacks; the animate list by SP2001's labels (a person, an animal). For the native check: the spoken forms each table accepts (also) and those it leaves out because they are another case's form (the doc's list)
meta.about: The forms book of word forms (companion/README.md, "Word forms"; bridge/src/forms.ts). tables: hand-checked forms of everyday irregular verbs, by slot (pres.1sg … imp.2du), each replacing Wiktionary's forms of the word (sl.json merges homographs: biti, to be, carries biti, to beat's bijem, bije; hoteti's table has odd rows), standard Slovene in forms, the spoken forms a native speaker says too (bojo, grejo, jejo, vejo, reko, mam) in also: accepted, never shown as the answer. partners: verbs that pair, pf the one done once (a movement, a whole act), impf the one going on (a state, again and again); kind position for a movement and the state after it (sesti, sit down: sedeti, be sitting), aspect for the same act once or going on (kupiti, kupovati); gloss: a meaning where the dictionary has none, or says more. leave_out: words whose forms aren't asked (stati: to cost, stanem, and to stand, stojim, share one entry). Nouns: a table (with its gender) for each noun Wiktionary gets wrong (a wrong accusative, gender or plural, two words merged in one entry); every other noun's forms are checked against its regular declension (bridge/src/noun-paradigm.ts: the fitting forms standard, the dictionary's old or dialect ones variants, a slot that doesn't fit never asked as a form to produce). animate: the masculine nouns naming a person or an animal, whose accusative singular is the genitive (vidim brata, psa), which Wiktionary can't be trusted on. A noun table's also: the other variants and the spoken forms (accepted, never shown); its variants: the old or dialect forms the regular check had found (brati beside bratu: accepted, labelled, never shown).
